rv.q: So are Shearsmith and Steve Pemberton now winding down? Not a bit, if Stage/Fright is any guide. From its murderous prologue on – hands-down the most memorable mobile phone announcement ever made in a theatre – this live show is as twisty and unpredictable as the best of their episodes on the BBC.

Expect everything you love from the shows here: accents, slapstick, wigs, false teeth. It’s old-school laughs that still do the trick. As one of the younger members of the crowd, I suspect a good few references went over my head.
...an evening that gives the audience a good laugh – and a valuable fright
Pemberton and Shearsmith seize on this — there is, of course, a ghost at Wyndham’s Theatre who needs to make an entrance.

Like so much else in this dazzlingly entertaining evening, don’t take that at face value. I do so hate to lose a reader, but if you have bagged a seat for this sold-out West End run, the best way to enter the theatre is as a blank slate.
...two-and-a-half hour stage send-off to their beloved horror anthology is a twisted joy

Things look promising at first. The duo initially turn their sharp-eyed nerdery towards the theatre world, blending together stories of Grand Guignol excess and haunted playhouses with clever sideswipes at contemporary shows, from the star casting and cheap thrills of 2:22 a Ghost Story to the video walkabouts that have become commonplace since ...
There is a nifty spin on the No 9 door, reallocated to a place in the auditorium. The audience is warned that terrible things happen in Wyndham’s, such as “Kenneth Branagh’s King Lear”.
Fans will enjoy unpicking its snarl of tangled entrails

Pemberton and Shearsmith are fine actors who really do get under the skin of their characters, but if I were an aficionado I’d still feel short-changed. Nor is there much to chuckle about in the limp hostage interlude, which will feature a different celebrity guest each night.
The BBC series Inside No 9 is a phenomenon.
Diehard fans are sure to be satisfied
Still inventive and fun but short on sharp shocks
